summary: BlueHarbor Logistics — realtime stream silence + retry-loop causing duplicate completions and billing spike (post-incident follow-up)
description:
Issue summary: Customer reported repeated silent streaming sessions where the server stopped emitting chunks after initial token output. Clients retried the request and platform returned duplicate completions for the same prompt, causing a billing spike and customer-visible duplicate messages.
Impact: Intermittent loss of streaming payloads for BlueHarbor's high-throughput telematics pipeline, duplicate completions seen in ~22% of affected sessions, billing surge estimated +14% for the customer during the incident window. Several downstream systems de-duplicated incorrectly, resulting in operational confusion.
Environment: Production (us-east), customer on enterprise plan with pin to redwood/gpt-3.8x-large, traffic via dedicated API key and routed through streaming-proxy pools with autoscaling enabled.
Timeline (high level): 2026-03-10 11:05 UTC - First customer alert to Support; 11:12 UTC - Triage and page to SRE; 11:20 UTC - Initial mitigation: temporarily disabled streaming proxy keepalive optimization; 11:45 UTC - Traffic routed to fallback pool (non-optimized kernel); 13:10 UTC - Duplicate completions observed to drop to <1%; 14:00 UTC - Customer confirmed service stability; 15:30 UTC - Incident declared resolved.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Create long-running streaming session with prefix size >2k tokens and KV cache reuse; 2) Simulate client network hiccup (socket close/reopen) after initial chunk; 3) Observe server behavior: either silence until client retries, or immediate replay of completion token stream leading to duplicate outputs; 4) Reproduce reliably when streaming-proxy had keepalive optimization enabled and serving-runtime kernel A selected.
Investigation notes: Early logs pointed to stream session state marked CLOSED on proxy but serving runtime still had active generation job; subsequent retry requests were not matched against previous job IDs due to an edge-case in session reconciliation. Trace IDs: trace-uh12-03, trace-uh12-04. Packet capture from proxy showed TCP close followed by SYN new session within 250ms. Kernel A (attention-optimized) was selected for low-latency customers; observed race in KV cache handoff under socket reconnect. Billing showed duplicate invoiceable completion events because generator job emitted finalization event twice when session reconciliation returned mismatched session token.
Root cause: A race condition in streaming-proxy session reconciliation plus an optimistic finalization path in serving-runtime kernel A. When the proxy fast-reclaimed session state on socket close while the generator was still finishing, a subsequent retry created a new session that triggered the generator to emit completion events again. The billing system counted both finalization events as independent completed responses.
Resolution and roll-forward: 1) Emergency mitigation: disabled keepalive-based fast-reclaim in streaming-proxy and added 500ms grace period for session reclaim (rolled at 11:20 UTC). 2) Rolled traffic to fallback kernel B that uses conservative finalization (11:45 UTC). 3) Hotfix PR merged to ensure generator finalization is idempotent (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1298) and to include session reconciliation token validation. 4) Billing adjuster script run to dedupe duplicate completion events for BlueHarbor and any other affected keys and credit invoices (completed 2026-03-12).
Post-incident actions: - Engineering will land additional unit tests around session reconnection and finalization idempotency (owner: Priya Nair). - Add a monitoring alert for anomalous completion duplication rate >0.5% per API key (owner: SRE). - Update runbook to include immediate rollback knob for streaming-proxy keepalive optimizations. - Conduct a targeted audit of other optimizer kernels for similar finalization behavior (owner: Runtime team).
Customer communications: Support sent initial status updates at 11:18/12:05/13:00 UTC. Customer requested detailed RCA and billing correction; follow-up call scheduled for 2026-03-14 16:00 UTC. Billing credit issued and reflected in customer's portal on 2026-03-12.
Notes: No PII was involved. No evidence of malicious intent or targeted attack. Related internal ticket INT-412 tracking longer-term kernel rework.
